# robots.txt and sitemap Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Ship a `robots.txt` that welcomes all crawlers and points at a generated sitemap, both carried to production by the existing deploy path.

**Architecture:** `robots.txt` is a static file in `public/`, which `astro build` copies into `dist/` verbatim. The sitemap is generated by the `@astrojs/sitemap` integration, configured with a `filter` that excludes the `os/<slug>/view.json` endpoints. `deploy/rebuild.sh` already copies all of `dist/` into the new release, so nothing under `deploy/` changes.

**Tech Stack:** Astro 4 (SSG), `@astrojs/sitemap`, Playwright for the end-to-end guard.

**Spec:** [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-09-robots-txt-design.md`](../specs/2026-08-09-robots-txt-design.md)

## Global Constraints

- The production origin is `https://desktopcolors.com` — already set as `site` in `astro.config.mjs`. The `Sitemap:` line and the sitemap's own `<loc>` entries use it verbatim.
- No per-crawler rules. One `User-agent: *` group, and `/api/` as the only `Disallow`. Do not add a blocklist, an allowlist, or `Crawl-delay`.
- Do not disallow `/os/*/view.json` in `robots.txt`. It is excluded from the *sitemap* instead, via the integration's `filter`.
- Nothing under `deploy/` is modified.
- `package.json` pins `astro: ^4.15.0`. The sitemap integration must resolve to a version that works on Astro 4 — `@astrojs/sitemap` **exactly `3.2.1`**, no caret.

## Corrections after execution

Executed 2026-08-09 (`a6574bf`, `3ec29b3`). Two of this plan's assumptions were wrong, and
the steps below are corrected in place; the deliverable is unchanged. Details and reasoning
in the spec's *Corrections after implementation*.

1. **Step 5/6 — the version.** `@astrojs/sitemap@^3` resolves to 3.7.3, which reads the
   Astro-5-only `routes` argument of `astro:build:done` and kills this Astro 4 build with
   `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'reduce')`. Pin `3.2.1` exactly. Step 6's
   `npm ls` check cannot catch this — the package declares no `peerDependencies` at all, so
   the tree looks clean either way. The build is the only real check.
2. **Step 7/9 — the `filter`.** It was never needed: the integration lists page routes
   only, so the 22 `view.json` endpoints stay out unaided (687 HTML pages → 687 `<loc>`).
   Step 9 is what proved it, by staying green when it was supposed to go red.

## A note on the test loop

The Playwright suite's `webServer` runs `npm run build && npm run preview`
(`playwright.config.ts`). A cold build of the ~704 pages takes roughly 130 seconds, so
every red/green cycle in Task 1 costs about that much. This is expected — do not switch
to a cheaper layer to avoid it. `robots.txt` and the sitemap only exist as build output,
and the vitest suites see no build output and no HTTP (`TESTING.md`, "The layers").

Run a single test rather than the whole file while iterating:

```bash
npx playwright test -g "robots.txt"
```

---

### Task 1: robots.txt, the generated sitemap, and the end-to-end guard

`robots.txt` and the sitemap ship together and are reviewed together: a `Sitemap:` line
pointing at a file that does not exist is worse than no line at all, so neither half is
independently shippable.

**Files:**
- Create: `public/robots.txt`
- Modify: `astro.config.mjs`
- Modify: `package.json`, `package-lock.json` (via `npm install`)
- Test: `e2e/smoke.spec.ts` (append one test at the end of the file)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `site: "https://desktopcolors.com"` from `astro.config.mjs`; the `request`
  fixture pattern already used by the `"serves a per-OS view.json with normalized detail"`
  test at `e2e/smoke.spec.ts:169`.
- Produces: `dist/robots.txt`, `dist/sitemap-index.xml`, `dist/sitemap-0.xml`. Task 2
  documents these.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

Append to the end of `e2e/smoke.spec.ts`. Note that it never fetches the absolute
`Sitemap:` URL — that URL points at production, and the test server is
`http://127.0.0.1:4321`. It asserts the origin and then follows only the **pathname**
against the local build. The same trick is used again for the `<loc>` inside the sitemap
index, so the test does not hardcode the `sitemap-0.xml` filename.

```ts
test("robots.txt welcomes crawlers and names a sitemap this build serves", async ({ request }) => {
  const res = await request.get("/robots.txt");
  expect(res.status()).toBe(200);
  const body = await res.text();

  // All crawlers welcome; the beacon endpoint is the only thing off-limits.
  expect(body).toMatch(/^User-agent: \*$/m);
  expect(body).toMatch(/^Disallow: \/api\/$/m);

  // The Sitemap line must be absolute and on the production origin...
  const line = body.match(/^Sitemap: (\S+)$/m);
  expect(line).not.toBeNull();
  const advertised = new URL(line![1]);
  expect(advertised.origin).toBe("https://desktopcolors.com");

  // ...and the path it names must actually be served. Fetch the path, not the
  // absolute URL: that one points at production, this test at the preview server.
  const index = await request.get(advertised.pathname);
  expect(index.status()).toBe(200);
  const indexXml = await index.text();
  expect(indexXml).toContain("<sitemapindex");

  // Follow the index to the actual URL set (never hardcode "sitemap-0.xml").
  const loc = indexXml.match(/<loc>(\S+?)<\/loc>/);
  expect(loc).not.toBeNull();
  const urlset = await request.get(new URL(loc![1]).pathname);
  expect(urlset.status()).toBe(200);
  const urlsetXml = await urlset.text();

  // It lists pages...
  expect(urlsetXml).toContain("https://desktopcolors.com/os/windows-95");
  // ...and not the JSON endpoints, which are not pages.
  expect(urlsetXml).not.toContain("view.json");
});
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run the test and watch it fail on the first guard**

```bash
npx playwright test -g "robots.txt"
```

Expected: FAIL at `expect(res.status()).toBe(200)` — received `404`. There is no
`robots.txt` yet.

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `public/robots.txt`**

`public/` is copied into `dist/` verbatim by `astro build`, so no Astro code is involved.

```
# desktopcolors.com
# Everything here is a public, static archive and is meant to be indexed.
# Deliberately minimal: no bot allowlist to go stale.

User-agent: *
Disallow: /api/

Sitemap: https://desktopcolors.com/sitemap-index.xml
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the test and watch it fail on the second guard**

```bash
npx playwright test -g "robots.txt"
```

Expected: FAIL at `expect(index.status()).toBe(200)` — received `404`. This is the
important intermediate failure: it proves the test actually follows the `Sitemap:` line
instead of just pattern-matching the file's text.

- [ ] **Step 5: Install the sitemap integration**

```bash
npm install @astrojs/sitemap@3.2.1
```

Exactly `3.2.1`, no caret — see *Corrections after execution* above. Confirm `package.json`
records `"3.2.1"` and not `"^3.2.1"`; `npm install` writes the caret by default and a later
`npm install` would then pull the Astro-5-only 3.7.x back in.

- [ ] **Step 6: Verify the resolved tree**

```bash
npm ls @astrojs/sitemap astro
```

Expected: `@astrojs/sitemap@3.2.1` and `astro@4.16.x`. Note that this proves less than it
appears to — the package declares no `peerDependencies`, so npm reports a clean tree for
incompatible pairs too. Step 8 is the real check.

- [ ] **Step 7: Register the integration in `astro.config.mjs`**

Replace the whole file:

```js
import { defineConfig } from "astro/config";
import preact from "@astrojs/preact";
import sitemap from "@astrojs/sitemap";

export default defineConfig({
  site: "https://desktopcolors.com",
  integrations: [preact(), sitemap()],
});
```

No `filter` — the integration lists page routes only. Carry the explanatory comment from
the committed `astro.config.mjs` (why no filter, why the exact pin) rather than
reconstructing it.

- [ ] **Step 8: Run the test and watch it pass**

```bash
npx playwright test -g "robots.txt"
```

Expected: PASS.

- [ ] **Step 9: Establish what the `view.json` assertion actually guards**

`TESTING.md` § T4 — a guard never seen failing is not known to work.

This step was written expecting the assertion to go red once the `filter` was removed. It
does not: the sitemap contains no `view.json` either way, which is how the filter was found
to be dead code. Confirm that for yourself rather than taking it on faith:

```bash
npm run build
find dist -name view.json | wc -l          # 22 endpoints exist
find dist -name '*.html' | wc -l           # 687 pages
grep -c "view.json" dist/sitemap-0.xml     # 0
grep -c "<loc>" dist/sitemap-0.xml         # 687
```

So the assertion cannot fail against the current dependency versions. It is kept as a
characterization guard: it is what fails if a future `@astrojs/sitemap` starts emitting
endpoint routes. The comment in `e2e/smoke.spec.ts` says so, so that the next reader does
not mistake it for a live guard on our own config.

- [ ] **Step 10: Run the full suite**

```bash
npm run check && npm test && npm run test:e2e
```

Expected: `astro check` clean, all vitest tests pass, all Playwright tests pass. `npm run
check` matters here specifically because Step 7 changed `astro.config.mjs`.

- [ ] **Step 11: Commit**

```bash
git add public/robots.txt astro.config.mjs package.json package-lock.json e2e/smoke.spec.ts
git commit -m "feat(seo): serve robots.txt and a generated sitemap

All crawlers are welcome; /api/ is the only Disallow, because the beacon
endpoint has nothing to crawl and a crawling GET lands in the error log.

The sitemap comes from @astrojs/sitemap, filtered so the per-OS view.json
endpoints are not advertised as pages. The e2e guard follows the Sitemap:
line's path rather than asserting a hardcoded one, so a mistyped path or a
dropped integration fails the build."
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Add the paragraph**

Match the surrounding style — a bold lead-in, then prose. Insert between line 175 and the
`### islands/` heading:

```markdown
**Crawler-facing output (`robots.txt`, sitemap).** `public/robots.txt` is copied into
`dist/` verbatim by `astro build`; it allows every crawler and disallows only `/api/`,
which serves the beacon and has no document to fetch. The sitemap is generated by
`@astrojs/sitemap` (`astro.config.mjs`) as `sitemap-index.xml` + `sitemap-0.xml`, which
the `Sitemap:` line in `robots.txt` points at. The integration's `filter` excludes
`/os/<slug>/view.json`: those routes are data for the island, not pages, and would
otherwise be advertised as indexable. Both artefacts reach production through the ordinary
`cp -R dist` in `deploy/rebuild.sh` — there is no deploy-side step. Reasoning:
[`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-09-robots-txt-design.md`](superpowers/specs/2026-08-09-robots-txt-design.md).
```
